Maya R: noticing a throughput dip on canary pool when routing to small-quant variants. batch sizes collapse to 1-2 requests more often, throughput down ~15%

Jon P: seen that. is it KV warmup or kernel selection thrash?

Maya R: both. KV hit rate drops ~18% when compat fallback triggers, because requests get split across kernel-incompatible variants. profiler shows ~40% more kernel loads per minute.

Liam C: do you have a pprof/flame link?

Maya R: https://perf.internal/redwood/pprof/17692 -- flame attached. key section: kernel_select() frequently called from route_compat_try() when compat set narrow.

Maya R: snippet:
```
if (!compat_match(a,b)) return fallback();
kernel = select_best_kernel(model_variant, seq_len);
if (kernel != last_kernel) reload_kernel(kernel);
```

Priya S: two quick ideas: 1) add short-lived variant affinity token (ms) to keep batches on same kernel; 2) widen compat predicate to allow kernel reuse across quant/arch minor diffs.

Jon P: affinity sounds promising. what's reasonable ms? 5-50ms window?

Liam C: measured latency SLO 50ms for short requests. 30ms affinity might help batches form without hurting tail.

Maya R: propose default queue policy tweak: prefer same-variant for up to 25ms OR until batch token budget reached. token_budget currently 256 -> consider bump to 384 for these routes.

Priya S: also add metric: kernel_reload_rate, compatset_entropy, kv_hit_rate_per_variant. we can alert on kernel_reload_rate > 0.1/sec/pool.

infra-bot: perf-regression-alert: pool-canary-3 kernel_reload_rate spike at 2026-03-10T10:12:03Z

Jon P: can we do an A/B canary: rule change only for routes with median seq_len < 128 and high qps?

Maya R: yes. will open rollout PR with config and perf dashboards. assigning to @Jon P for canary rollout and @Priya S for metric dashboards. :thumbsup:

Liam C: also test widening compatset to allow same kernel across quantization bit-flips (int8 vs int4) if kernel supports both; that reduces kernel churn a lot in sim.

Maya R: thanks all. I'll include a small microbenchmark and sample flame in PR. expected win: +12-18% throughput, +0.5ms median latency change.
